title: route-eject-incident-scratch
body:
High-level: quick personal scratchpad for the 2026-02-27 multi-region routing incident where requests from EU region were abruptly ejected to US region (higher latency) even though capacity existed in eu-west-1. Trying to capture commands I ran, logs I saw, and hypotheses to iterate on. Notes to self — incomplete, unpolished.

Timeline (rough):
- 2026-02-27 09:18 UTC: Pager alert - elevated 95th latency for /v1/generate in eu-west-1.
- 2026-02-27 09:21 UTC: Spike in model-variant-swaps and routing errors observed in routing-proxy logs.
- 2026-02-27 09:30 UTC: Automated canary fallback triggered; large fraction of traffic routed to us-east-1 variant.
- 2026-02-27 10:02 UTC: Manual mitigation - pinning to model x.y.z in eu cluster. Latency partially recovered but spike recurred at 10:40.

What I checked (commands + outputs):
- quick curl to routing admin to see route table snapshot:
  curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \n    'https://routing-admin.internal/api/v1/routes?region=eu-west-1' | jq '.routes[] | {id, policy, capacity, last_updated}'
  -> sample line: {"id": "svc/generation:eu-west-1", "policy": "smart-route:v3", "capacity": "120 rps", "last_updated": "2026-02-27T08:59:12Z"}

- routed request logs (proxy):
  [2026-02-27T09:20:53Z] req_id=abc123 client=svc-a region=eu-west-1 route=smart-route:v3 outcome=EJECT reason="latency_budget_violation" backend=us-east-1-variantB
  [2026-02-27T09:20:54Z] req_id=abc124 client=svc-a region=eu-west-1 route=smart-route:v3 outcome=OK backend=eu-west-1-variantA latency_ms=82
  Observation: mixed outcomes within same minute — suggests per-request decisions, possibly due to sampling or stale telemetry.

- routing-proxy metrics (prom query):
  curl -s 'http://prom.internal/api/v1/query?query=sum(rate(routing_ejects_total[1m])) by (region,reason)'
  -> eu-west-1: 18 (latency_budget_violation), eu-west-1: 3 (capacity_exceeded), us-east-1: 2 (manual_fallback)

- checked kv cache for route policy TTLs in redis:
  redis-cli -h redis-routing-01 TTL route:smart-route:v3:eu-west-1
  -> 320 (seconds)
  redis-cli GET route:smart-route:v3:eu-west-1:metadata
  -> "{\"policy\":\"smart-route:v3\",\"last_reeval\":\"2026-02-27T09:18:45Z\"}"
  Note: reeval timestamp lines up with initial spike. Need to confirm whether reeval triggered by bad telemetry.

- k8s describe of routing-proxy pod that handled some ejections:
  kubectl -n infra describe pod routing-proxy-5fd9c | sed -n '1,200p'
  -> Events show several 503s to telemetry-sink around 09:18 which could make recent latency numbers stale.

- tcpdump on host (sanitized):
  tcpdump -i eth0 -nn "port 5005" -c 200
  -> lots of retransmits and a handful of 3-way handshake retries to telemetry.sink.internal:5005 around spike time.

Error snippets and traces I copied:
- routing-proxy: "WARN smart-routing: decision ejected request for route svc/generation:eu-west-1; telemetry_age_ms=54000 > max_age_ms=12000"
- fallback-controller: "INFO policy-evaluator: fallback candidate selected us-east-1-variantB (score +0.72)"
- model-host eu node: "ERROR kv-cache: failed to fetch prefix cache: timeout after 250ms"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Telemetry lag (telemetry sink hiccup) caused the policy evaluator to mark eu variants as stale, triggering ejection to fallback regions. Evidence: telemetry_age_ms in logs, tcp retransmits to telemetry sink.
2) Brief network partition between eu regional router and model hosts leading to transient 5xx which policy treated as capacity_outage. Evidence: kubectl events showing 503s + model-host kv-cache timeouts.
3) Bug in smart-route:v3 where an edge case multiplies eviction score if latency_age > threshold AND recent error sample exists (double-counting). Evidence: mixed OK and EJECT for same minute — could be a race in per-request enrichment.
4) Configuration drift: TTLs for route policies renewed incorrectly after deploy on 2026-02-26; stale metadata flagged as old. Evidence: redis TTLs and last_reeval timestamp cluster around 09:18.

Actions I ran / quick mitigations attempted:
- Bumped telemetry-sink replicas (k8s scale) and restarted one telemetry forwarder: kubectl scale deploy telemetry-forwarder --replicas=4 -n infra
- Forced route policy reeval in admin: POST /api/v1/routes/reeval?route=smart-route:v3&region=eu-west-1 -> immediate drop in ejects for ~8 minutes
- Pinned routing decision to prefer local region for 10m via admin toggle:
  curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://routing-admin/internal/api/v1/override -d '{"route":"svc/generation","region":"eu-west-1","force_local":true,"ttl_s":600}'
  -> observed drop in ejections but unsure if this masks root cause.

Remaining unknowns / follow-ups:
- Is telemetry sink having intermittent network issues between eu zones and the sink instance? Need to check cloud provider logs, VPC flow logs for packet loss.
- Which component marks telemetry_age for routing decisions? Is it the policy-evaluator service (separate pod) or routing-proxy local cache? Trace the code path.
- Validate if policy-evaluator uses multiple telemetry sources and whether one stale source can cause ejection despite fresh local metrics.
- Re-run unit test that covers old_telemetry + single-error-sample to see if double-counting exists.

Notes to self (actionable):
- Add test for telemetry_age gating + error-sample weighting in smart-route:v3 (PR idea: add guard that requires >N fresh samples before applying ejection).
- Expand telemetry forwarder SLOs doc (link above) to include expected TCP retransmit thresholds.
- Create quick dashboard showing telemetry_age distribution vs ejection rate by region.
- For postmortem: correlate route reeval events with deploys and redis TTL changes (deploy on 2026-02-26 flagged earlier).

Quick reproduction attempt (manual):
- Simulate telemetry lag by delaying ingestion: drop packets to telemetry.sink:5005 from eu-forwarder-host for 60s and watch ejection rate. Use iptables to DROP on telemetry sink port locally, then remove.
  sudo iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 5005 -j DROP; sleep 60; sudo iptables -D OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 5005 -j DROP
- Observe routing-proxy logs during this window to confirm telemetry_age behavior.

References and quick links:
- INC ticket: INFRA-1147 (alerts + timeline)
- Routing admin endpoint docs: https://internal-docs/redwood/routing-admin
- Telemetry forwarder repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-forwarder

Open questions for Lina/Ethan:
- Lina: can you pull VPC flow logs for eu-west-1 between 09:00-09:30? Searching for RSTs/retransmits to telemetry.sink.
- Ethan: can you grep policy-evaluator logs for 09:18-09:25 and paste any "telemetry_age_ms" entries?

Random scratch bits:
- Might be worth adding a small jitter before policy ejection to avoid synchronized ejections when telemetry ages spike across many proxies.
- Consider a slow-fail path where a single stale telemetry source cannot override local health signals.

Next steps (short):
1) Confirm telemetry sink network health and forwarder logs.
2) Add a dashboard and run the iptables simulation in staging.
3) Draft a patch to add guard in smart-route:v3 (unit + integration test).
4) Postmortem write-up draft (link to be added).

-- Maya

(End of quick scratch doc)
